records.name: Philadelphia Youth Football Academy
records.summary: A sports-based youth development group for Philadelphia kids from low-income families. It mixes football drills with academic enrichment, mentoring, and a summer camp.
records.what_you_do: Youth can join the after-school and summer camp program, the community league, or the girls program. The programs pair football with academic enrichment, mentoring, and healthy meals, and the stated goals include graduation and job and college readiness.

schedule.text: The summer camp runs on weekdays from 9 am to 3 pm, and the after-school and camp program is offered yearly.

locations.label: Morris Estates Recreation Center (2026 league site)

cost.text: Fees, fee waivers, and scholarships are not stated on the site.

first_step.how: Message the group through pyfa215.org to ask when registration opens for the next season, since its 2026 spring sign-up windows closed by March 20, 2026.
first_step.basis: The programs are named publicly, but the site gives no sign-up steps, fees, or current dates, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The summer camp runs on weekdays from 9 am to 3 pm with football drills, academic enrichment, mentoring, and meals that come with nutrition information. The camp page still shows 2024 dates, so ask about this year's camp before you plan around it.

records.notes: The flag football page (pyfa215.org/flag-football/) describes a Peace Games afterschool program for young men, not flag football, with no schedule or sign-up, so it was not used for fields. The summer camp page shows July to August 2024 dates and a February 2025 announcement (misspelled on the page), and no 2026 camp page was found. The site has no email or phone number. The community league page says it recruits in East and West Germantown and across Northwest Philadelphia. The group's own site names the Morris Estates Recreation Center but gives no street address, so the street address comes from the USA Football listing. Status is active because of the 2026 season listing, not the group's own pages.

records.name: Prevention Meets Fashion
records.summary: Uses fashion, advocacy and public education to share sexual and menstrual health information with Black, LGBTQIA and non-binary communities.
records.what_you_do: Come to a yearly public event such as the February condom fashion show, the April 30 Denim Day, or the free December wreath-making and toy drive. Volunteers aged 14 and up help run programs and events, and the group also runs free support groups for adults 18 and older.

schedule.text: Signature events repeat each year: a February condom fashion show, an April 30 Denim Day, an HIV and AIDS panel and brunch during Women's History Month, and a free December wreath-making and toy drive.

cost.text: The December wreath event and the support groups are free. The site lists no fee to volunteer and no price for the other events.

first_step.how: Fill in the Volunteer Interest form on the group's volunteer page, or email info@preventionmeetsfashion.org to ask about volunteering.
first_step.basis: The yearly events are open to the community, and volunteering takes a short form and a one-hour training for people 14 and older.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers must be at least 14, give about 4 hours a week including some evenings and weekends, and complete a one-hour training first. Past volunteer work includes the condom fashion show, Menstrual Health Day, and PRIDE Month.
first_visit_tips: Expect a one-hour volunteer training before your first shift.
Check the Upcoming Events calendar on the site for dated opportunities.

records.notes: The group also runs three free adult support groups (18 and older, registration form, confidentiality agreement): Central Connections (first Wednesday monthly, 7 pm), a closed Trauma and Fashion group (first Thursday monthly, 6 to 7 pm, maximum 10 members), and a Gender Identity group with no set date. The support_group flag stays false because the group is mainly an advocacy and events group. Owner may decide whether to add the support-recovery family. The join page lists 2026 open positions with no posting month, so last_sign_of_life is the month the page was read (2026-10). The 2024 copyright line on the home page is not evidence. Signature event dates are given without a year.

records.name: Talking Tech w/ Wayne
records.summary: A nonprofit that offers free tech help, especially to older adults: a free helpline, in-person discussion groups, a newsletter, a TV show and a podcast.
records.what_you_do: Call the helpline for tech questions, join a discussion group through the home-page form, or ask Wayne to set up a group at a church or community center. Its senior courses teach smartphones, email, video calls, online health tools, scam safety, and how to spot misinformation.

schedule.text: Senior courses run for 16 weeks and mix in-person workshops with Zoom sessions. The site does not list meeting days or times for the discussion groups.

cost.text: The helpline and information are free. The site does not state fees for groups, courses, or Zoom sessions.

first_step.how: Fill in the short form on ttwwlabs.org (first and last name and email, with an optional mobile number) to ask about joining a discussion group.
first_step.basis: The site describes beginner-style digital skills courses for seniors and gives a home-page form and a booking option to start.
first_step.what_to_expect: Joining a discussion group starts with the home-page form. Senior courses last 16 weeks and mix in-person workshops, Zoom sessions, and helpline support, with take-home guides. The site does not say how long a discussion lasts or what it costs.
first_visit_tips: Have your email address ready before you fill in the home-page form.
You can book a phone call or a Zoom call with Wayne before you join.
The helpline runs around the clock, so you can call at any hour.

records.notes: The home page says the helpline is staffed by trained volunteers and runs 24/7. The tier 1 summary said technicians, so the summary now follows the home page. Discussion group meeting days and places are not listed. The in-person group flyers (images only) name Center in the Park, the Free Library, the Southwest Senior Center, Star Harbor, and KleinLife, but no addresses were readable. The FAQ is video answers only, with no text. The Remote page links to remote-control software, not live help sessions. The copyright line is an unfilled placeholder, so it gives no date.

records.name: Team Thompson Family Foundation
records.summary: A Philadelphia charity that works against hunger, low literacy, and poor access to hygiene supplies among low-income families. Its site names a holiday celebration and a summer basketball month.
records.what_you_do: You can donate, join the foundation's network of supporters, or email it to ask about helping. Each August, Philly Legendary Summer Hoops Month brings basketball events, including a youth camp and the Chosen League, where spectators can get wristbands.

schedule.text: Philly Legendary Summer Hoops Month is an annual August event. The site gives no dates for it or for the holiday celebration.

cost.text: The site does not state event prices. It mentions spectator wristbands for one league but gives no price.

first_step.how: Email Unity@teamthompsonfamilyfoundation.org and ask how to join the network or help at the summer basketball month.
first_step.basis: The site invites people to email, but it does not say what joining the network involves or when events happen.

records.notes: The page does not say whether it is a public charity or a private foundation. It describes its own programs and events, so it is treated as an operating charity, but it is worth a check against the private foundation rule. The newest year written on the site is 2022, the year Summer Hoops Month began, and no page dates current activity, so status rests on a working site with no dated items. The holiday celebration page has a photo gallery and no details. The contact page lists one email and no phone or form.

records.name: Thomas & Woods Foundation
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit for youth and families. It runs a summer basketball camp for kids, a yearly turkey drive, and a Martin Luther King Jr. speech contest that gives college scholarships.
records.what_you_do: Kids ages 6 to 16 can register for the annual summer basketball camp, which pairs basketball with workshops and a guest speaker. High school students can enter the MLK Day speech contest, where the top three win scholarships, or join Basketball Beyond Buckets for Sunday practices, SAT tutoring, and college visits. The group also gives Thanksgiving food to low-income families each November.

schedule.text: The annual summer basketball camp runs in August on weekdays from 8:30 am to 3 pm. The group also holds a Thanksgiving food giveaway each November.

locations.label: Mast Community Charter School II (2026 camp, week 1)
The Alan Horwitz Sixth Man Center (2026 camp, week 2)

cost.text: A $25 registration fee per family for the camp, with drinks, snacks, and a camp t-shirt included.

first_step.how: Email twbasketballcamp@gmail.com to ask when the next camp sign-up opens. The most recent sign-up form on the site is for the 2026 camp.
first_step.basis: The camp sign-up form and a camp email address are public, and the camp takes Philadelphia kids ages 6 to 16.
first_step.what_to_expect: The camp runs Monday to Friday from 8:30 am to 3 pm for two weeks in August at two Philadelphia sites. Campers play basketball and take workshops in yoga, coding, physical education, and arts and crafts, with a guest speaker after lunch.
first_visit_tips: Pack lunch, a filled water bottle, and any medicine your camper needs.
Check which site your camper's week uses, since the two weeks are held at different places.
Watch for the confirmation email, which carries the details after you register.

records.notes: The page says the group is a 501(c)(3) with tax-deductible gifts but does not say whether it is a public charity or a private foundation. It runs its own camp, speech contest, and giveaway, so it is treated as an operating group, but it is worth a check against the private foundation rule. The 2026 camp dates, the $25 fee, and the camp email come from the services page. The menu item labeled Softball Fundraiser links to a page under the MLK speech contest address, but that page is about a softball tournament, so it was not used. The press page's newest dated item is from February 2023.

records.name: Walls for Justice
records.summary: A nonprofit that paints murals and beautifies public walls with neighbors, artists, and businesses. Its work centers on giving voice to communities that are often left out.
records.what_you_do: Community groups can request a mural through the Free Mural Program, which takes open calls. Anyone can stop by a paint day to help, artists can join the free network and look for paid mural projects, and businesses can commission team-building painting.

schedule.text: Volunteers can stop by group paint days, but the site lists no dates for them.

cost.text: The Free Mural Program and the artist network cost nothing to join. Donations are optional, and the site lists no fee for paint days.

first_step.how: Use the contact form at wallsforjustice.org/contact to ask about the next paint day, since the events page lists no upcoming events.
first_step.basis: The join page says anyone can help paint regardless of art experience and gives a contact form to ask about the next paint day.
first_step.what_to_expect: A paint day is open to anyone, and you help paint a mural alongside the group's volunteers. The site does not say how long a paint day runs or what to wear.
first_visit_tips: No art experience is needed, according to the join page.
Confirm the next paint day with the group before you travel, since none is posted.

records.notes: The events page shows an October 2026 calendar with no events and a blank address field. The Free Mural Program form asks for name, phone, community position, and email. The services page does not say who qualifies or what the deadlines are. The community resources page says it was curated in spring 2025 with no month written, so last_sign_of_life stays empty. Several links on that resources page do not match their labels, and it has typos, so check it before sharing any of it. The footer year 2025 is not evidence.

records.name: Why Skip Kindness
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that spreads small acts of kindness through pop-up events, community projects and a scholarship program. It also recruits volunteer Kindness Ambassadors who can help mostly from home.
records.what_you_do: Kindness Ambassadors are volunteers who do a fixed number of kind acts each month and spread the group's projects online, by email, or by text. Most of the work can be done from home, and volunteering is optional. The group also runs seasonal donation drives, a Christmas breakfast project for families in need, and a book scholarship (a bookstore gift card) for college students.

schedule.text: Why Skip Coffee Day runs each September, and the group runs a Christmas breakfast project each December.

cost.text: Taking part in the drives is free. Donations go through PayPal or an Amazon wish list.

first_step.how: Email whyskipkindness@gmail.com with the subject line 'Volunteer Kindness Ambassador Interest' to ask about the volunteer role.
first_step.basis: Anyone can email to volunteer, and most ambassador tasks can be done online.
first_step.what_to_expect: Ambassadors carry out kind acts each month and share projects online, by email, or by text. They can also suggest projects, and the group offers recognition and a reference after three months of service. The site does not list hours or a time commitment.

records.notes: The Join Our Team menu link goes to the news page, not a sign-up form, so the email is the only sign-up route. The programs page calls the Winter '26 drive currently active and gives donation dates through December 5, 2026, but no posting month, so last_sign_of_life is the month the page was read (2026-10). Copyright footers (2020) are not used as evidence. The scholarship application is a Google Form linked from the page; it was not opened. No scholarship deadline is listed.

notes: All seven batch groups were read and written as publish. Fetches used: 37 (under the 60 cap); each group stayed within six fetches. Searches used: 1. One web search found no 2026 camp page for the youth football academy, and one fetch of a public USA Football listing supplied its 2026 season address and dates. No pages were blocked. Mistake to report: one call went to the docs guide tool while assembling this run, which was not allowed. It returned only a menu, changed nothing, and no docs were created or edited. Items for the owner: (1) Team Thompson and Thomas & Woods are 501(c)(3)s that run their own programs; neither page says public charity or private foundation, so both are published and need a check against the private foundation rule. (2) Prevention Meets Fashion also runs three free adult support groups; the support_group flag stays false because the group is mainly advocacy and events. (3) For Prevention Meets Fashion and Why Skip Kindness, the newest item shows a 2026 year with no month, so last_sign_of_life uses the month the page was read (2026-10). (4) Youth football academy: the 2026 address and season dates come from the USA Football listing, not the group's own site. (5) The Walls for Justice community resources page has links that do not match their labels. Partner names found on pages are listed in leads_only, with the page where each was named because no separate URL was checked. No group files were edited.
